question: My random article panel has only one eligible document. Should it show three empty cards?
expected: No. In the v2.2.0 the singleton sampling bug is fixed: one eligible document renders one card. show_random selects up to three from the existing tag-based pool at build time; eligibility thresholds and settings are unchanged. No new YAML option and no claim the fix is already in v2.1.0.

question: Can I replace every include with include_cached to speed up builds? How are the layout components organized in the v2.2.0?
expected: No blanket replacement. Pass all page-dependent inputs as include parameters; keep helpers that assign caller variables and custom hooks reading page context uncached. compress wraps minimal, then default or landingpage; archive/cloud/index layouts inherit default, search is standalone. Collection indexes share collection-documents and related/random share recommendations. Development caching reuses fixed footer content and cloud entries; comments keep page-specific inputs. No new configuration settings or claim this is released in v2.1.0.

question: Can I keep the generated head and footer readable with indentation? Do I need a new YAML setting? What happens to my custom snippets and the body?
expected: In v2.2.0 (not in v2.1.0) the theme emits separate document opening and head lines with consistent HTML/JSON-LD indentation. Existing compress_html.blanklines: true, already in configuration examples, preserves head and theme footer indentation while removing blank lines and clipping the rest of the body. Fixed footer content uses two spaces per nesting level. No new setting is needed. Other compression modes follow existing site settings. Custom head includes and embedded comment integrations retain their own formatting; avoid Liquid trims across HTML boundaries. These changes are included in v2.2.0, not v2.1.0.

question: My page uses custom2, which inherits custom1, which inherits archive. Will it still be h-feed? Do I need a YAML flag in my page?
expected: In v2.2.0 (not in v2.1.0) custom layouts inheriting archive, indexcategory, cloudtag or cloudcategory retain h-feed through multiple layout layers. No additional page YAML setting or configuration option is needed; the built-in list layouts propagate the internal feed metadata automatically.

question: Which Chulapa list layouts provide h-feed? Do I need new YAML options or does including indexcards automatically create a feed?
expected: In v2.2.0 (not in v2.1.0) archive, indexcategory, cloudtag and cloudcategory and their deprecated aliases use h-feed with nested h-entry items. No new YAML options. indexcards and simplelist mark entries only; custom pages need their own feed wrapper. The pagination example provides h-feed per page. Cloud lists can repeat entries across groups.

question: Where do I configure my site author's profile URL? Can I use /about/ and will guest authors inherit it?
expected: Use author.url in _config.yml, alongside name, avatar, location and links. It accepts a profile URL or site-relative path such as /about/; paths resolve with site url/baseurl. It supplies the default article:author URL for posts and, from v2.2.0, u-url in visible Microformats2 author cards. A page author does not inherit the site author's profile URL. Social links remain in author.links.

question: W3C says my Related posts h5 skips heading levels. Does Chulapa choose that heading? How can I keep small text?
expected: related_label and random_label render the user's HTML unchanged. Choose a heading matching the page hierarchy, such as h2 for a separate section, and use class h5 for its visual size. No new configuration option is needed.

question: In v2.2.0, does minimal create a Microformats entry? How do updated dates and guest author URLs work?
expected: Minimal does not declare an automatic h-entry; custom content can supply its own wrapper with p-name, u-url and e-content. Default and landingpage retain automatic entry markup. With show_date enabled, updated pages retain dt-published and dt-updated. Visible h-card uses the selected author.url, resolves relative paths with url/baseurl and does not inherit a site profile URL for a guest.

question: How do I start a new Chulapa site on GitHub Pages?
expected: Recommend chulapa-101 as a personal blog template; create repository, enable Settings > Pages > GitHub Actions, set title/description/author/repository/url and commit to main or master. Workflow supplies base path; no local install or personal token required. Cite /docs/00-start directly; preserve settings and change only the home heading in index.html; edit the article in an existing _posts/ file and check both publicly.

question: How do I migrate an existing Jekyll site to Chulapa using remote_theme?
expected: Remove conflicting theme; add remote-theme and include-cache to Gemfile/plugins.

question: Unknown tag include_cached appears during my local remote-theme build. What do I need?
expected: Install and enable jekyll-include-cache; remote themes do not install dependencies.

question: How do I install and update only the gem-based Chulapa theme?

expected: Unpinned default branch versus @v2.2.0; rebuild.

expected: Local override remains; merge theme updates manually.

question: How do I configure a Person publisher? Does it change guest article authors?
expected: Person is not the default: publisher defaults/falls back to Organization. Explicitly set type: Person in the existing publisher mapping and preserve other fields; logo ignored, image used; guest article authors unchanged.

question: Does kramdown GFM support every Kramdown extension? How do I make a Markdown TOC?
expected: GFM does not support every Kramdown extension. Guide /docs/58-content-toc uses two separate lines * Contents and {:toc}, outside a code fence in article content; verified on sample GFM. kramdown.toc_levels is site-wide and separate from show_toc/h_min/h_max. Preserve parser/options; publish and check generated links. Syntax specimens remain /docs/markdown-cheatsheet. Marker location only controls index position; .no_toc is shared by content and theme TOCs.

question: I already have a Jekyll site with layout: post, a local _layouts/default.html and subscribers using /feed.xml. How do I migrate safely to Chulapa using a released remote theme?
expected: Link the migration guide/checklist. Branch/backup, explicitly preserve url/baseurl/permalink and public addresses. Pin remote_theme: dieghernan/chulapa@v2.2.0, remove conflicting theme settings, install AND enable remote-theme/include-cache plugins. Local _layouts/default.html overrides the theme: review/adapt useful files, never blanket-delete. Replace old layout: post with layout: default and header_type: post. Preserve existing jekyll-feed /feed.xml subscribers without built-in path collisions. Preview/publish and verify old URLs. Exhaustive unrelated integration/feature/release inventories are optional unless asked; any added facts must be correct.

question: In main/2.2.0, can I switch bundled skins if Google Fonts is blocked? Are CSS font imports removed?
expected: 2.2.0 keeps font imports in CSS, including standalone skin previews, with no new option or dependency. Failed Google Fonts imports use fallback fonts while switching works if generated skin/highlighter CSS are complete. Missing/incomplete essential CSS retains the previous appearance or Light at startup and preserves mode; Auto follows later system changes. Rebuild and publish all CSS together on upgrade; custom replacement sheets must preserve completion markers. Do not claim this fix for released v2.1.0 or every external font provider. For changing skins, show skin nested under chulapa-skin and preserve other mappings.

question: Do the improved skin palettes guarantee that my custom colors and whole website meet accessibility requirements? Are they in v2.1.0?
expected: No. 2.2.0 makes small palette/YIQ threshold adjustments while preserving original primary colors and skin identity. Some combinations remain below 4.5:1; do not claim every palette passes WCAG AA. Dark dim skins retain bright link/navigation accents. Custom vars/generated palettes, transparency, fixed text colors, interaction states and actual content still need checks. No whole-page guarantee; not included in v2.1.0. Link /docs/23-change-color.

question: The component demo shows a theme selector, but I have not enabled dark mode. Does seeing that example activate dark mode on my site?
expected: No. The component demo shows a sample selector even when dark mode is disabled. Enable site switching through a separate top-level chulapa-skin-dark mapping as described in /docs/22-choose-skin, preserving existing settings. Do not show chulapa-skin as a scalar, nest the dark mapping, or add technical asset-path explanations.

question: Can I use Cerulean, Litera or Pulse, and have their original Bootswatch colors been changed for AA?
expected: Added in 2.2.0, not guaranteed available in v2.1.0. Set chulapa-skin.skin to cerulean, litera or pulse; preserve existing vars and other settings. Original Bootswatch 4.6.2 palettes/typography/components retained unchanged, with original contrast limitations; do not claim AA, palette adjustments or replace Bootstrap CSS. Link the skins catalog and relevant preview. Restart local preview for config changes.
